class.name: ClimateRecipe
class.description: Climate of a terrain: temperatures and seasonal lapse rates, the linear theory of orographic precipitation (Smith and Barstad 2004) over a wet-day wind rose, the rain-snow threshold, mean cloud cover for the sun, and the grid the maps are baked on. See docs/ideas/terrain-generation.md, "Climate maps".

members.member: Mean cloud cover, 0 to 1, for the shortwave (Kasten and Czeplak 1980).
Extra ground around the data map's square to include, m, so horizons and the precipitation see mountains just outside it.
Time for cloud water to form precipitation, s.
Standard deviation of daily mean temperatures around the month's mean, K, for the snow fraction.
Share of the rain that runs off in the month it falls (McCabe and Markstrom 2007: 5% typical).
Time for precipitation to fall out, s. With [member conversion_time] it sets how far rain drifts downwind (about wind speed times their sum).
Ground reflectance for light reflected from surrounding terrain.
Share of the stored soil surplus reaching the rivers each month (a linear groundwater reservoir; 0.5 in McCabe and Markstrom 2007). Lower keeps rivers fuller through dry months.
How far horizons are traced for shading, m. 0 leaves terrain shadows out (the slope still faces the sun or not).
Temperature drop with height in January, K/km. Surface lapse rates are lower in winter (about 4 to 5 in the Alps) than in summer (Rolland 2003).
Temperature drop with height in July, K/km.
Latitude in degrees: sun path, day lengths and the Coriolis term of the precipitation model. Negative south of the equator.
Snowmelt per positive degree day with no sun, mm/day/K (Hock 1999).
Moist buoyancy frequency of the air, 1/s (0.005 in Smith and Barstad 2004).
Precipitation on flat ground away from terrain, mm a year.
Cell size the precipitation model is solved at, m; upsampled to [member sun_cell].
Share of the background precipitation the deepest rain shadow keeps: showers and fronts the linear model leaves out still reach the lee.
Month of the most precipitation with [member precipitation_seasonality], 0 January to 11 December.

How unevenly the year's precipitation falls: 0 the same each month, 1 none in the driest month (a harmonic peaking at [member precipitation_peak_month]). Used by the water balance of [member TerrainGenerator3D.climate_recipe].
Extra snowmelt per positive degree day per W/m² of the month's shortwave, mm/day/K (Hock 1999): sunny slopes melt out first.
Air temperature where half the precipitation falls as snow, C (1.0 on average, Jennings et al. 2018).
World height where [member temperature_january] and [member temperature_july] hold.
Water the soil holds for plants, mm (Thornthwaite and Mather 1957; 150 mm in McCabe and Markstrom 2007).
Cell size of the climate grid, m (every map except precipitation is computed at it).
Upwind distance for Winstral Sx, m (100 in Winstral et al. 2002).
January mean air temperature at [member reference_height], C.
July mean air temperature at [member reference_height], C.
Share of the year's hours with precipitation; the hours the terrain lifts moist air.
Prevailing direction the wet-day wind blows from, degrees clockwise from north (270: westerly).
Wind speed on wet hours, m/s.
Standard deviation of wet-day wind directions around [member wind_from], degrees; 360 or more for no prevailing direction.
